text:
andrew: Quick thought — our current compact-on-idle behavior is hurting tail latency for short bursts. When a GPU goes idle we kick off aggressive slab compaction which races with a new incoming request and spikes p99.

maria: +1 saw this in the 04:30 incident repro. What's your concrete proposal?

andrew: Proposal sketch: introduce a tunable 'defrag window' (default ~250ms) that defers heavy compaction while treating small bursts specially. Two modes: 'defer' where compaction is postponed, and 'background' where low-prio compaction runs only when util<10% and no inflight requests. Also attach a backpressure token so long-running compaction can be preempted by allocation hotpath.

sophie: I like the window idea. We should tie it to recent-interarrival-rate rather than absolute idle time. If bursts are >X qps in last 1s, shorten window to 50ms. Use SLO signal (tail-latency breaches) to autotune.

lee: Important: define the allocator<>evictor interface clearly. Something like: allocator.request_guard(duration_ms, reason, priority_hint) -> guard_id; evictor.yield_if_preempted(guard_id) -> bool. That way the allocator controls short-term defer, evictor can still make progress when it's safe.

andrew: Exactly. Minimal API: 
```
// request a short defrag-suppression window, returns a token the evictor can check
string request_defrag_guard(int ms, int priority_hint);
// evictor polls: should_preempt(token) -> true|false
```
This avoids heavy locking on allocation hotpath.

maria: Telemetry we need to track: compaction_start, compaction_duration_ms, compaction_bytes_moved, preempt_count, guard_waits, burst_interarrival_p90/p99, p50/p95/p99 tail for small requests. Also record tenant when tuning per-tenant.

sophie: One more prefetch-fidelity note: when we prefetch KV/attention pages during cold requests, prefer probabilistic prefix prefetch (only hot spans), avoid full kv pulls for short contexts. We should expose a hint from request: `prefetch_profile: "short|medium|long"`.

lee: Rollout plan: 1) implement guard API + metrics, 2) default window 250ms as experiment, 3) canary to 5% tenants with telemetry, 4) add autotune based on tail-latency and burst rate, 5) full rollout. Include a kill-switch config flag.

andrew: Ops knobs I'd add: `--evictor-defrag-window-ms`, `--evictor-background-threshold-percent`, `--evictor-max-preempt-ms`. Defaults sensible but overridable per-tenant.

maria: Minor: ensure compaction preemption isn't leaky (partial compaction must leave consistent slab state). We need a safe checkpoint/undo plan if compaction stops mid-chunk.

andrew: Agree — chunked compaction + idempotent markers. We'll draft a small RFC for allocator/evictor token semantics and compaction choreography.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: /infra/checks/defrag-window-RFC-1832109876 — 5 checks pending :clipboard:

sophie: For the RFC include simple perf microbench: 100ms bursts every 500ms vs continuous load and measure p99 and cost. If p99 improves without cost blowup, good to ship.

lee: I'll prototype guard API tomorrow and post a tiny PR for review. tagging @maria @andrew for follow-up. :thumbsup:

andrew: Thanks — agreed on next steps. I'll add the metric names to our telemetry backlog and start the RFC doc.
